reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents a baby-food chart and recipes for young children, with ordinary cooking instructions such as measured ingredients, sauteing vegetables, and seasoning steps. The subscribe prompt, social-media branding, and health disclaimer are consistent with routine recipe-channel engagement and informational content rather than a money, credential, investment, or external-scheme solicitation.

citations.quote: Food Chart 1-2 Years Baby Along With 35 Recipes | Complete Diet Plan & Baby Food Recipes For 1-2 Yr
Food Chart 1 - 2 Years Baby | Complete Diet Plan & Baby Food Recipes for 1 - 2 Years | Baby Food Recipes
For cooking for 3 minutes on high heat, it became dry.

opening.argument: The video is structured around directing viewers into an external engagement and contact network rather than merely presenting a self-contained recipe. Its description prominently lists WhatsApp, Facebook, Instagram, Pinterest, YouTube, and Twitter links, then expressly asks viewers to “like” and “subscribe.” That establishes an action-oriented promotional pathway. Although no cash reward is stated, the combination of multiple external destinations and a direct engagement request leaves the viewer being steered toward participation without explaining what they receive for doing so. The apparent cooking subject therefore does not eliminate the possibility that the content is primarily a low-barrier acquisition funnel for audience attention.

citations.quote: Like And Follow Us On: WhatsApp https://www.whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaCVXqwGU3BMfjlOyL18 Facebook – https://www.facebook.com/shecooksNbakes/
Please like, and subscribe to my channel!

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the recipe title and cooking footage as dispositive, but those materials establish only the surface theme. They do not explain why the description distributes viewers across numerous external platforms or why engagement is specifically requested. The disclaimer also shifts responsibility to viewers rather than substantiating the safety or reliability of the advice. Thus, ordinary-looking food footage can coexist with a promotional acquisition objective.

citations.quote: Food Chart 1-2 Years Baby Along With 35 Recipes | Complete Diet Plan & Baby Food Recipes For 1-2 Yr
Viewers are subjected to use this information at their own risk.
Please like, and subscribe to my channel!

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted links and subscription request show ordinary channel promotion, not a reward, payment, registration fee, withdrawal process, or promised asset. The evidence never says viewers receive money or anything valuable for clicking, following, or subscribing. A broad social-media presence and a responsibility disclaimer do not convert recipe content into a scam.

citations.quote: This is not a sponsored video.
I am not a health practitioner.
Please like, and subscribe to my channel!

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: the description supplies a dense list of external links, directs viewers to another YouTube channel for more baby food, and includes a broad disclaimer that viewers use the information at their own risk. The video also presents itself as a “Complete Diet Plan” for young children while expressly stating that the creator is not a health practitioner. That combination creates a credibility gap: the material is packaged as comprehensive guidance, yet responsibility and potential harm are disclaimed. The result is a promotional presentation that can attract trust and off-platform attention without equivalent accountability.

citations.quote: Complete Diet Plan & Baby Food Recipes For 1-2 Yr
For more Baby food visit: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCN2qud5gVdtFZR2my3wpgkg/videos
I am not a health practitioner.
Viewers are subjected to use this information at their own risk.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the disclaimer routine overlooks its significance when the title uses comprehensive language about a child’s diet. The defense cites cooking steps, but ingredient preparation does not validate the nutritional claims implied by a complete plan. Nor does it address the unusually broad collection of external links and the invitation to continue elsewhere. Those signals warrant treating the presentation as potentially deceptive promotion rather than harmless instruction.

citations.quote: Complete Diet Plan & Baby Food Recipes For 1-2 Yr
For more Baby food visit: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCN2qud5gVdtFZR2my3wpgkg/videos
I am not a health practitioner.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are not scam-specific red flags. The title identifies recipes and a food chart, while the description expressly says the video is not sponsored and warns that the creator is not a health practitioner. No large return, payment, investment, reward, or deceptive verification claim appears. A cautionary disclaimer is evidence of limitation, not evidence of fraud.

citations.quote: This is not a sponsored video.
I am not a health practitioner.
Please make sure your baby is not allergic to any of the ingredients used in this recipe.

opening.argument: The cooking format functions as promotion for a branded channel and its wider network. The footage repeatedly displays the “she cook’s” branding, while the end card combines the channel identity, multiple social-platform icons, and “Subscribe to our channel.” The description reinforces that role by listing several social accounts and directing viewers to additional videos. The recipes are therefore not presented solely as neutral information; they are the vehicle used to build an audience and move viewers toward the creator’s external properties. That promotional steering is enough to raise scam concerns even though the solicitation is framed as lifestyle content.

For more Baby food visit: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCN2qud5gVdtFZR2my3wpgkg/videos

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense identifies the apparent subject but not the content’s distribution strategy. Repeated branding, an end-card subscription request, and links to several external accounts show that the recipe is also an audience-acquisition vehicle. “Not sponsored” addresses paid sponsorship, not whether viewers are being directed into a promotional network. The ordinary format should not obscure that steering function.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Branding and subscription prompts establish a creator promoting its own cooking channel, which is ordinary self-promotion, not a scam. The frames show food preparation, including measured ingredients and cooking steps, while the description identifies recipes and provides a safety warning. Nothing links following or visiting the channels to a reward, payment, investment, or asset acquisition.
